overview.description: Bezique is the aristocratic ancestor of Pinochle, a trick-taking and melding game for two players. Historically favored by Winston Churchill, it is played with a 64-card deck (two 32-card decks stripped). Players score points by declaring melds like 'Bezique' (Queen of Spades + Jack of Diamonds) and 'Royal Marriage' (King + Queen of Trumps) after winning tricks. The game is a race to 1000 points, characterized by a unique 'Trick-and-Draw' phase where hands are constantly refilled.

history.origins: Developed in France in the early 19th century from the game 'Piquet' and 'Briscan'. The name might come from the Italian 'Bazzica'.
timeline: 1860s: Sweeps through London and Paris society as the fashionable game for couples.
1910s: Superseded by Bridge and Pinochle in popular culture.
1940s: Famously played by Winston Churchill during WWII to relax.
Present: Remains a classic 2-player game for traditionalists.
history.evolution: The game expanded into multi-deck 'Rubicon Bezique' (4 decks) and 'Chinese Bezique' (6 decks), increasing the scores into the thousands.
history.cultural: Evokes a sense of Victorian elegance. The markers used are often elaborate wooden pegs.

setup.players: Two players only. The standard two-handed game is played head-to-head; players cut for deal with the highest card having preference (rank order A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7). No partnerships.
setup.deck: 64 cards. Take two 52-card decks, remove all 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s, and 6s. Combine remaining. Start with 8 cards each.
setup.dealing: Deal 8 cards to each player (3-2-3). Turn the next card for Trump. Place the remaining deck (Talon) face down.

rules.objective: First to reach 1000 points via Melds and Trick 'Brisques' (Aces and Tens).
rules.gameplay: Phase 1 (The Draw): 1. Non-dealer leads. 2. You do NOT need to follow suit. 3. Winner of trick captures cards. 4. Winner *declares one meld* (places face up on table) if possible. 5. Both draw back up to 8 cards. Phase 2 (The End): When the stock is empty, players pick up their melded cards. Rules change: Must follow suit, must win trick if possible.
keyRules: You can only declare a meld AFTER winning a trick.
Cards used in a meld remain on the table but can be played to subsequent tricks (breaking the meld).
A card can be used in multiple different melds but not the same meld twice without re-melding.

strategy.basic: Hoard Queens of Spades and Jacks of Diamonds. The Double Bezique (500) is the game-winner. Do not waste them in tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Stock Management: Keep track of how many cards are left. You want to win the LAST trick of Phase 1 to declare one final meld before the rules tighten.
strategy.advanced: Breaking Melds: Sometimes you must play a component of a meld (e.g., an Ace from 4 Aces) to win a trick to declare a bigger meld (Sequence). It's a trade-off.
tips: The 7 of Trumps (Dix) can be swapped for the turned trump card (scoring 10 pts).

list.name: Rubicon Bezique
list.description: 4 Decks (128 cards). Game is not played to a score but for total points over 4 deals.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rubicon Bezique is described conceptually, but detailed engine overrides for its multi-deck scoring and deal structure are not yet encoded.

difficulty.easy: Wins tricks randomly. Declares simple marriages. Does not count the talon.
difficulty.medium: Saves Bezique cards. Swaps the 7 Dix card. Counts Aces and Tens.
difficulty.hard: Perfect Meld Tracker. Knows exactly if a Double Bezique is impossible based on opponent plays. Adjusts strategy to Phase 2 transition.

considerations: Must handle the two-phase transition where rules change radically.
Tableau cards must be tracked separately from hand cards for meld logic.

ante.reason: Bezique is a point-based melding game and does not utilize a monetary or chip-based ante.

deal.reason: The initial distribution of eight cards per player and the talon setup is handled by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: The talon is a face-down stock; the only public card is the trump proposal turned up at the start.

buy_market.reason: Players acquire new cards by drawing from the talon for free rather than purchasing from a market.

buy_stock.reason: Drawing from the talon is a free mandatory phase action and does not involve a purchase cost.

fold.reason: Both players must participate in the dual-phase trick play until all 64 cards have been played.

check.reason: The game uses a trick-taking and melding structure rather than a vying structure with checks.

call.reason: There is no pot or bet to match in Bezique; competition is based on point accumulation.

bet.reason: Success is measured by points on a scorecard rather than through financial or chip-based betting.

raise.reason: There are no wagering rounds in Bezique, so the value of the deal cannot be increased via raises.

declare.description: Declare a meld sequence (Marriage, Bezique, etc.) after winning a trick.
declare.constraints: Only available to the winner of the previous trick during Phase 1.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private until played; melded cards are displayed publicly on the tableau.

award_pot.reason: Winning is determined by cumulative match points rather than by awarding a physical pot.

play_card.description: Play a card from your hand to the current trick.
play_card.constraints: Phase 1: Any card. Phase 2: Must follow suit and win if possible.

draw.description: Draw one card from the talon to refill the hand to eight cards.
draw.constraints: Only during Phase 1 after each trick.

discard.reason: Every card in the hand must be played into a trick; no cards are discarded to a waste pile.

pass.reason: Players must always play a card to every trick; passing a turn without action is not allowed.

bid.reason: The trump suit is determined by a random flip rather than through a bidding auction.

meld.description: Form a valid point-scoring combination on the table.
meld.constraints: Must win a trick immediately prior to the declaration.

go_out.reason: The game terminates only after the talon is exhausted and the final eight tricks are played.

drawSources.notes: Talbot draw after each trick in Phase 1.

notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are played directly to tricks or held in melds; no discard pile is utilized.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: The 7 of trumps (Dix) allows a swap action but does not trigger automated engine effects.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Melds are announced and placed openly on the table; no hidden tokens are required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Bezique is a trick-and-meld game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: The goal is point accumulation through melds rather than being the first to empty the hand.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Phase 2: Must win trick if possible.

meldConfig.initialMeldRequirement: Must win a trick to declare.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Phase 1: No restrictions. Phase 2: Must follow suit.

customActions.description: Distribute eight cards to each player and turn up the trump card.
Place a valid meld combination on the table for points.
Exchange the seven of trumps for the turned trump card.
Take the top card of the talon into the hand.
Play a card following strict suit and trump rules.
Sum all meld points and brisques to determine the winner.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; card rank comparison (A=11, 10=10, K=4...) determines trick wins.
engine.deckDescription: Two standard 32-card decks combined (64 cards total): eight ranks (seven through ace) in each of four French suits, duplicated. No jokers; used for Bezique where marriages and sequences score and only one trump suit is active.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs) in duplicate (two 32-card packs). One suit is trump; marriages (king and queen of trump) and bezique (queen of spades and jack of diamonds) score. Follow suit when able.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit in each deck: seven, eight, nine, ten, jack, queen, king, ace. In trump the order is jack, nine, ace, ten, king, queen, eight, seven. Point values: ace 11, ten 10, king 4, queen 3, jack 2; others zero.
engine.dealPattern: Eight cards to each player clockwise; one trump turned.

hero.title: BEZIQUE
hero.subtitle: The Queen & The Jack
hero.tagline: Two decks. One obsession. The search for the 500-point Double.

synthesis.shortDescription: The classic game of melding and trick-taking. Famous for its 'Double Bezique' hand—two Queens of Spades and two Jacks of Diamonds—which awards a massive 500 points. Elegant, thoughtful, and deeply rewarding.

prompts.human: You just won a trick with the Ace of Trumps. You have a Queen of Spades on the table from a previous Marriage declaration, and a Jack of Diamonds in your hand. Declare 'Bezique' now! Place the Jack next to the Queen for 40 points.
prompts.ai: Game: Bezique. Phase: 1. Rules: A>10>K. Melds allowed after trick win. Bezique = Q(S) + J(D). Double Bezique = 2xQ(S) + 2xJ(D).

scoring.description: Points are scored immediately upon declaration.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach 1000 total points.

penalties.Last Trick: Winning the final trick of Phase 2 awards a 10-point bonus.

scoring.splitRules: If both reach 1000 in the same hand, the player with the higher total wins.
